descriptionChirho: To take counsel with oneself or others, to deliberate, resolve, or form a plan of action. Middle voice βουλεύομαι predominates in the NT, emphasizing personal deliberation. Cross-linguistically convergent: Arabic تشاور/قصد (consult/intend), German beschliessen (resolve), Spanish deliberar/planear, Hebrew התיעץ/החליט (take counsel/decide), Korean 모의하다/계획하다 (plot/plan), Hindi योजना बनाना/सोचना (make plans/think), French deliberer. John 11:53 and 12:10 (the chief priests and Pharisees plotted/deliberated to put Jesus and Lazarus to death). 2 Cor 1:17 (when I planned this, did I plan according to the flesh? -- repeated βουλεύομαι emphasizes the act of deliberating). Luke 14:31 (a king going to war will sit down and consider/deliberate whether he is able). Acts 27:39 (they were planning/deliberating to run the ship aground). All occurrences share the core sense of purposeful mental deliberation leading to a decision or plan.
